keyTakeaways: Three well-run Halloween ideas beat eighteen; most of the 18 here cost under $100 by our estimates, and each comes with one metric to watch.
Go visible on 1 October: in a 2024 pilot survey of 62 people, most treated 1–31 October as the accepted window for Halloween items.
Weight the final 48 hours: in our nearest analogue, Raksha Bandhan 2026 (n = 89), 86.1% of on-time pages were built within 24 hours of the day.
CAN-SPAM has no B2B exception and each violating email can cost up to $53,088, per the FTC; honor opt-outs within 10 business days.
Contest hashtags need the word "contest" or "sweepstakes" in them, per the FTC's Endorsement Guides FAQ; "sweeps" probably isn't enough.

faqs.question: When should a small business start Halloween marketing?
faqs.answer: Plan in mid-September, about six weeks out, and go visible on 1 October. A 2024 pilot survey found most people treat 1–31 October as the normal window for Halloween items, so a display in early September can look premature. Put your heaviest push into the final 48 hours before 31 October.

faqs.question: What are cheap Halloween promotion ideas for a small shop?
faqs.answer: A customer-voted pumpkin window ($20–$60), a costume-day discount, a build-the-window video and a two-email sequence to your existing list all cost under $100 by our estimates. A seasonal sticker on your existing bags runs about $25–$60 for 500 and replaces themed packaging.

faqs.question: Do I need to label a Halloween photo contest on Instagram?
faqs.answer: Yes, if entrants post to win something. The FTC's Endorsement Guides FAQ says a hashtag like #XYZ_Rocks is not enough; one that includes "contest" or "sweepstakes" should be, and "sweeps" probably is not. Ask entrants to put it at the start of the post.

faqs.question: Can I use a famous horror movie name in my Halloween promotion?
faqs.answer: Avoid it. The USPTO explains that trademarks protect words, phrases and designs that identify goods, and copyright protects movies and music, so a poster built around a film title or its character art can raise both. Describe the genre instead, such as "witchy movie night".

faqs.question: Does CAN-SPAM apply to a small business Halloween email?
faqs.answer: Yes. The FTC's compliance guide says the law has no exception for business-to-business email, and each violating message can cost up to $53,088. Include your postal address and a working opt-out, honor opt-outs within 10 business days, and keep the subject line truthful.

faqs.question: How do I measure whether my Halloween marketing worked?
faqs.answer: Pick one metric per idea before you start: till transactions against a normal weekday, email click rate against your average, contest entries, or code redemptions. Write the numbers down on 1 November, while you still remember what you ran, so next October starts from evidence.

faqs.question: Does a limited-edition Halloween product actually sell better?
faqs.answer: Scarcity tends to create urgency: a 2026 survey of 121 online shoppers found perceived scarcity strongly predicted a sense of urgency (β = 0.787). The authors caution that the two measures overlap, and the tactic only holds up if your stated quantity and end date are real.

faqs.question: What should I do about customers who don't celebrate Halloween?
faqs.answer: Offer a one-click way to skip Halloween emails without leaving your list, and make any discount available without a costume. Keep Día de los Muertos (1–2 November) separate rather than folding it into Halloween, because it is its own tradition.

faqs.question: Should a B2B company bother with Halloween marketing?
faqs.answer: Only lightly. A personal thank-you to a few key clients, or a staff costume photo, fits better than a discount campaign. If you email, CAN-SPAM still applies, since the FTC says it makes no exception for business-to-business messages.

faqs.question: Can I use SubhSandesh's Halloween page to promote my business?
faqs.answer: No. It is a one-person greeting page with no mailing list, coupon or reach. It works for thanking one loyal customer or staff member personally: you add photos, a letter and a question of up to 60 characters, and get an email the first time they answer.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Halloween Marketing Ideas: 18 Small-Business Plays by Channel

The Halloween marketing ideas that pay off for a small business are cheap, local and loaded into the last 48 hours before 31 October. Our nearest measurement of occasion timing is Raksha Bandhan, not Halloween, and the sample is small: of 89 festival pages built on SubhSandesh in 2026, 49.4% were made on the day itself and 86.1% of the on-time ones within 24 hours of it. Whatever you send will also be read on a phone, since 48.3% of the pages shared through SubhSandesh are opened on one.

Below are 18 Halloween promotion ideas grouped by channel, each with effort, estimated cost and the metric to watch, then a calendar working back from 31 October and the FTC, CAN-SPAM and trademark rules that catch small shops out.

## What is a Halloween marketing idea for a small business?

A Halloween marketing idea is a promotion that borrows the holiday's costumes, pumpkins and trick-or-treat ritual to give customers a reason to visit or buy before 31 October. For a small business it should cost under about $200 and run on staff you already have.

The date never moves: Saturday 31 October 2026, Sunday 31 October 2027. On a weekend Halloween your costume day and the trick-or-treat route land on a busy trading day.

## 18 Halloween marketing ideas by channel, with cost and the metric

Costs are our estimates in US dollars, before your own time. Pick three ideas, not eighteen.

### In-store and window

- **Customer-voted pumpkin window.** Staff carve three pumpkins; customers vote with a token jar at the till. Effort: low. Cost: $20–$60. Watch: till transactions against the same weekday two weeks earlier.
- **Trick-or-treat stop.** Put a sign on the door for the 31 October route and keep non-food treats (stickers, pencils) for children with allergies. Effort: low. Cost: $40–$100 for 200 treats. Watch: treats handed out, and opted-in sign-ups at the door.
- **Costume-day discount.** "Come in costume on 31 October, 10% off." Effort: low. Cost: the margin. Watch: discount redemptions at the till.

### Email

- **Two-send sequence.** One preview email about ten days out, one last-chance email on 30 October. Effort: medium. Cost: $0 on a list you already have. Watch: click rate against your normal average, and unsubscribes.
- **"Skip Halloween" opt-out.** Before the season, offer a one-click way to skip holiday emails without leaving the list. Effort: low. Cost: $0. Watch: how many take it, which tells you how much of your list does not celebrate.
- **Limited-run drop.** Announce a numbered batch with a real end date. Effort: medium. Cost: stock. Watch: sell-through by date.

### Social

- **Build-the-window video.** Film the display going up, start to finish. Effort: low. Cost: $0. Watch: saves and shares, not likes.
- **Costume photo contest.** Entrants post with a branded hashtag that includes the word "Contest"; the prize is a $25–$100 gift card. Effort: medium. Cost: the prize. Watch: entries, and follows during the contest window.
- **Staff or pet costume vote.** Post four staff or shop-dog costumes; followers pick. Effort: low. Cost: $0–$40. Watch: comments.

### Local partners and community

- **Shop-hop map.** Five neighboring businesses share one printed map; children collect a stamp at each door. Effort: medium. Cost: $30–$80 printing, split. Watch: completed maps returned.
- **School or library sponsorship.** Fund the prizes at a local costume parade in exchange for a flyer with a unique code. Effort: low. Cost: $50–$200. Watch: code redemptions.
- **Costume swap drop-off.** Collect outgrown costumes in early October; give them away the week before. Effort: medium. Cost: $0. Watch: first-time visitors.

### Loyalty and customer list

- **Double points, 24–31 October.** Effort: low. Cost: the points. Watch: repeat-visit rate against last October.
- **"Trick or treat" envelope.** Hand every buyer a sealed envelope worth 5–20% off a visit between 1 and 14 November. Every envelope wins something, which keeps it a discount rather than a prize draw. Effort: low. Cost: $15 printing plus the discount. Watch: November redemption rate.
- **One personal thank-you.** A handwritten card or a short personal message to your single most loyal customer. Effort: low. Cost: $0–$5. Watch: nothing; it is not a campaign.

### Packaging

- **Seasonal sticker.** Seal existing bags and boxes with a pumpkin sticker instead of buying themed packaging. Effort: low. Cost: $25–$60 for 500. Watch: tagged posts showing the package.
- **Numbered limited edition.** "200 made, sale ends 31 October." Scarcity works through urgency: in a 2026 survey of 121 online shoppers, [perceived scarcity strongly predicted a sense of urgency (β = 0.787)](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13404449), while social proof had a weaker effect. The authors flag overlap between the two measures, and the claim only holds if the number is true. Watch: sell-through.
- **Handwritten note in online orders.** One line, shipped 20–31 October. Effort: medium. Cost: $0. Watch: reviews and replies.

## Halloween marketing calendar: working back from 31 October

Start too early and the window looks odd. In a 2024 pilot survey of 62 people, most general respondents wore Halloween items [between 1 and 31 October and were complimented for it](https://www.iastatedigitalpress.com/itaa/article/id/17484/), while keen fans who started earlier more often heard "A bit early for Halloween, yeah?"

- **About six weeks out (mid-September):** choose three ideas, order limited stock and stickers, and check every name you plan to use.
- **1 October:** window goes up; contest opens; "skip Halloween" link goes into your regular email.
- **About 20 October:** preview email; shop-hop maps printed and shared.
- **24 October:** double points start; build-the-window video posted.
- **30 October:** last-chance email.
- **31 October:** costume day and trick-or-treat stop.
- **1–14 November:** envelope redemptions; write down what each metric did.

Weight your effort toward the end. In the Raksha Bandhan data above, only 6.7% of pages were built four or more days ahead. That is a different festival and a sample of 89, so treat it as a direction, not a forecast.

## Which Halloween promotion channel costs least per result?

This table compares four channels on cost, prep time, metric and the nearest SubhSandesh measurement.

| Channel | Est. cost | Prep time | Metric | Nearest SubhSandesh measurement |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Email sequence | $0 | 2–3 hours | Click rate | 48.3% of shared pages opened on a phone |
| Window and costume day | $20–$160 | 1 day | Till transactions | 86.1% of on-time Raksha Bandhan pages built within 24 hours |
| Social contest | $25–$100 | 3–4 hours | Entries | 11.1 average views per shared page |
| Personal thank-you | $0–$5 | 20 minutes | Reply | 90.9% of started pages are published and shared |

The cheapest result is the email you already have permission to send. Our measurements describe personal greeting pages, not shop promotions, so read the last column as behavior to plan around, not a benchmark.

## Halloween promotion rules: contests, email and character names

Three US rules, plus one of taste, trip small businesses every October.

**Contests.** The FTC's [Endorsement Guides FAQ](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/ftcs-endorsement-guides-what-people-are-asking) says a hashtag like #XYZ_Rocks does not tell readers a post was entered for a prize. Putting "contest" or "sweepstakes" in it, such as #XYZ_Contest, should be enough; "sweeps" probably is not. Tell entrants to put it at the start of the post. Prize draws that require a purchase raise state lottery-law questions, which is why the envelope above guarantees every buyer a discount.

**Email.** The FTC's [CAN-SPAM compliance guide](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/can-spam-act-compliance-guide-business) makes no exception for business-to-business email. Each violating message can cost up to $53,088. You must include a valid postal address and a working opt-out, honor opt-outs within 10 business days, and keep subject lines truthful, so a fake "Your order has shipped" subject is out.

**Character names.** The USPTO explains that a [trademark protects a word, phrase or design](https://www.uspto.gov/trademarks/basics/trademark-patent-copyright) that identifies goods, while copyright covers movies and music. A poster naming a famous horror film, or using its character art, can touch both. Describe the genre instead: "witchy movie night", not the franchise.

**Taste.** UK supermarkets made national news for selling "escaped mental patient" costumes. Kelly and Riach, writing in the [Journal of Business Ethics in 2018](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10551-018-3945-8), use that case to describe Halloween retail as stuck in a cycle of commercial "offense-contrition-offense": products pulled, apologies made, then the next one. Skip any theme that mocks illness, ethnicity or a real tragedy.

## Not everyone celebrates Halloween: build in an opt-out

Some customers skip Halloween for religious or personal reasons. Others mark Día de los Muertos on 1–2 November, a separate tradition, not a Mexican Halloween. The 2024 pilot study cites earlier work finding that people judge the timing of holiday promotions more favorably when they plan to celebrate, so the same email lands worse with someone who does not.

Offer the "skip Halloween" link from idea five, make any discount available without a costume, and keep anything at a child's eye level spooky-cute, with no gore.

## Thanking one loyal customer: where the Halloween page fits, and where it doesn't

[Our Halloween page](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween) is a one-person greeting page, not a marketing tool: no mailing list, no coupon, no reach. It fits the "one personal thank-you" idea above, for a regular or a staff member.

You add their name, a letter, up to six photos and a word to carve on the pumpkin, then send a private link. They knock three times, carve the jack-o'-lantern, read your letter by flashlight and answer a question you can rewrite (up to 60 characters, "Will you be my boo?" by default). Choose the bestie mode. You get an email the first time they answer, and they keep a 1080×1920 Boo License.

One quirk: the No button runs away a few times, which suits a friend more than a client. If you want to say thanks out loud, [the premium Halloween page](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween-premium) adds a voice note of up to 60 seconds and a reply box that emails you one reply of up to 280 characters.

Where it loses: the interface is English only, and it does nothing for a crowd. For 200 customers, a CAN-SPAM-compliant email is the right tool.

## Sources

- Federal Trade Commission, "CAN-SPAM Act: A Compliance Guide for Business", August 2023 (penalty edited January 2024).
- Federal Trade Commission, "FTC's Endorsement Guides: What People Are Asking", September 2017, updated July 2025.
- United States Patent and Trademark Office, "Trademark, patent, or copyright" (no publication date).
- Kelly, S. and Riach, K., "Halloween, Organization, and the Ethics of Uncanny Celebration", Journal of Business Ethics, June 2018.
- Smith-Glaviana, D. and Shields, D., "Fashion Countdown to Halloween", ITAA Annual Conference Proceedings, January 2024.
- Pal, S. and Milfelner, B., "From Scarcity Cues and Social Proof to FoMO", Behavioral Sciences, July 2026.

structuralLimitations: No US Halloween shopping-timing source was usable: NRF (the usual source, and what Amazon Ads' timing claim rests on) is at the batch cap, and the Think with Google Halloween page found is MENA 2022 data. The calendar rests on the ITAA 2024 pilot (n = 62, dress timing, not shopping) plus the Raksha Bandhan lead-time analogue (n = 89), both disclosed in the body.

BRIEF said FTC guidance on 'contests/sweepstakes': the FTC material actually fetched covers contest DISCLOSURE (hashtags) in the Endorsement Guides FAQ. 'No purchase necessary' / lottery law is state law, not FTC; the body says only that purchase-required prize draws raise state lottery-law questions, with no citation.
All idea costs are our own estimates in US dollars, labelled as such; no sourced price list was fetched.

First-party facts are platform-wide greeting-page data (phone-open share, views per page, publish rate) and Raksha Bandhan lead time; facts.md has no Halloween or business-use data. The table's last column is labelled as behaviour to plan around, not a benchmark.

auditReport.honestAssessment: Every top-10 page is a list of ideas or famous brand campaigns; none gives cost, effort and a metric per idea, and none states the FTC contest-hashtag rule, CAN-SPAM's $53,088 per-email penalty and no-B2B-exception, a trademark caution or an opt-out for non-celebrants, so an answer engine has specific, verifiable lines to lift here. It cannot overcome the authority of Amazon Ads and the marketing-SaaS incumbents, and its first-party numbers are greeting-page data used as analogues, not business results.
